newsitem.title: USA: Prosecutors seek life term for rampaging NY man.
newsitem.headline: Prosecutors seek life term for rampaging NY man.

text.p: Prosecutors will seek a life sentence rather than the death penalty for a New York man charged with killing one woman and beating two others in an eight-day rampage last summer, officials said Tuesday.

An attorney for 22-year-old drifter John Royster, who pleaded not guilty in July to charges of murder, attempted murder, robbery, assault and rape, said Royster's psychiatric condition apparently played a part in the decision.
"It is clear that he is a severely disturbed young man," said attorney Daniel Gotlin. "Of all the doctors who examined him, nobody felt he was malingering."

Police said Royster confessed to the June 11 murder of Park Avenue dry cleaning store owner Evelyn Alvarez, 65, the beating and sexual assault of a young pianist in Central Park June 4 and an attack on another woman while she was walking in Manhattan June 5.
The brazen daylight beating of the woman in Central Park drew national attention as she lay in a coma for two weeks after the attack and has since made a dramatic recovery.

Manhattan District Attorney Robert Morgenthau said in a statement that he would ask for a sentence of life without parole instead of capital punishment, which was reintroduced in New York in September 1995.
"This will ensure that the defendant, if convicted of murder in the first degree, will never again be a threat to law-abiding citizens," said Morgenthau, who declined any further comment.
Royster showed no emotion when the decision was announced in Manhattan Supreme Court. His next court appearance has not yet been scheduled.
The victims and their families had said Royster should not face the death penalty because of the high costs of capital punishment cases and their desire that he be forced to live with his conscience.
Royster also faced charges that he beat a woman comatose and sexually assaulted her on a footbridge late at night on June 7 in Yonkers, north of New York City.
